newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss ABB has optimistic outlook.
newsitem.headline: Swiss ABB has optimistic outlook.

text.p: ABB Switzerland, the Swiss country unit of electrical engineering group ABB Asea Brown Boveri AG, said it was optimistic about the future based on the 35 percent increase in new orders in the first six months of the year.

Alois Sonnenmoser, chairman of ABB Switzerland's management committee, also said in a statement the recent weakening of the Swiss franc against the dollar would have a positive impact on the company's financial result with a certain time lag.
"Looking at the 35 percent increase in orders received, my outlook for the future is optimistic," Sonnenmoser said.
He added measures to improve competitiveness were on schedule, but suppliers would also have to demonstrate willingness to develop joint solutions.
In the first six months of 1997, ABB Switzerland's net profit fell 19 percent to 112 million Swiss francs, while orders rose 35 percent to 3,057 million. Revenue fell eight percent to 2,380 million.
"Revenues and earnings in the first half of 1997 reflect the disappointing level of orders received in the prior year," ABB said.
